title: RoPEMover: Depth-Aware Object Relocation via Positional Embeddings
claim: One unified framework handles many editing tasks with realistic, scene-consistent results, shown through a gallery of before/after examples.
layout: 5 titled panels in a grid, image pairs left-to-right, dashed boxes mark edits
description: A dense gallery of photographs under a headline sentence that highlights in red the geometry-aware object motion method and diffusion transformer representations. Five rounded panels are titled 1. Object Placement, 2. Image Enhancement, 3. Depth Placement, 4. Object Removal and 5. Handling Occlusion. The large Object Placement panel at the top has two rows of before/after image pairs: a lantern on a dock, a bicycle on a wet street, a chair, a toy car, a sculpture, a basketball and a sled. Dashed blue boxes and red arrows mark the source region and the intended motion. Image Enhancement shows reference objects composited into scenes. Depth Placement shows triplets in which an object moves in front of or behind another. Object Removal pairs show removed items, with a red mask on the input. Handling Occlusion pairs show objects moving behind or in front of others. The eye goes first to the large top panel.
caption: Our method enables realistic object displacement in a single image while correctly handling occlusions, revealing unseen regions, and preserving shadows and reflections. By extending RoPE to a depth-aware formulation, we explicitly control object ordering, allowing placement in front of or behind other scene elements. Beyond motion, the same framework supports downstream edits such as object removal and adding objects to a scene, achieving consistent illumination, shadow casting, and overall scene integration.
abstract: Moving an object in a single image requires geometry-consistent spatial rearrangement, including handling occlusions, revealing previously unseen regions, and maintaining coherent shadows and reflections. Existing approaches are not well suited to this setting and often fail to preserve such scene-level consistency. We address this problem by introducing a geometry-aware object motion method that operates directly on the positional representations of diffusion transformers. Our key insight is that rotary positional embeddings (RoPE) define a structured spatial field that can be explicitly manipulated to induce controlled motion. We extend 2D RoPE into a depth-aware formulation that encodes 3D spatial structure, enabling consistent object displacement and scene-aware updates. Our model is trained using synthetic data combined with a small set of real images via parameter-efficient fine-tuning. Despite minimal real supervision, it preserves object identity under large spatial displacements, generates plausible content in newly revealed regions, and consistently updates scene-dependent effects such as shadows and illumination. Experimental results on standard object motion benchmarks demonstrate state-of-the-art performance across all evaluation metrics.
